release_changes: New FlashInfer KDA prefill with radix-cache checkpoint destinations; eligible safe-gate KDA now auto-selects it on SM100/SM103. Base Kimi config has gate_lower_bound=-5 and head_dim=128. Triton remains an explicit control.

Kimi shared experts now explicitly shard over full TP when their output is reduced over full TP; grouped/replicated EP cases are explicit. Most material to differing dense-attention TP vs full TP topologies, not proof of an ordinary TP8 speedup.

KDA value head width uses linear_attn_config.head_dim instead of MLA v_head_dim. Both equal128 in the audited K3 pins; no numerical difference is predicted for these exact configs from that one-line fix.
Fused front buffers reject quantized weights with separate scales; source guards prevent losing those scales. ROCm-specific weight conversion paths must not be described as B300 acceleration.
ModelOpt MegaMoE preserves canonical W13 gate/up ordering even when nominal runner is TRT-LLM; explicit layout guard added. This does not qualify a mixed-Kimi MegaMoE topology.
DSpark commit injection masks uncommitted full-attention token slots before cache lookup. Greedy proposal is now an explicit opt-in; old sampling environment switches are deprecated no-ops.
Scheduler speculative recurrent-state tracking accounts for grammar-retained committed lengths; include structured-output prefix resume/cancel cases in external validation.
Kimi Responses and Messages preserve inline system instructions through the native encoder; validate a mid-history instruction and prefix reuse through the KServe API route.

vllm.assessment: Release keeps `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` support and adds the opt-in latency-specialized decode (#61868); its source gate requires capability 10.3, MRV2, exactly TP4 without DP/EP/DCP, DSpark without adaptive verification, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, fp8 KV and MXFP4 indexer; the DSpark-draft half (#61869) is open. The FULL-graph prefill fix (#59986) and trailing-assistant prompt fix (#62729) are main-only: run DSpark with `enable_adaptive_verification:false` (as the recipe B300 presets do; issue #59970 reports an illegal memory access with `true` + `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` on 2×B300 TP2) and test trailing-assistant request shapes at the gateway. Recipe B300 cells were measured on 0909 weights; KServe startup probes must allow `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` 3600-7200 s. The NVIDIA NVFP4 export still needs open #61530.

sglang.assessment: `configs/deepseek_v41.py` is present, but the cookbook at `297e54f` still says V4.1 has not shipped in a CUDA release and selects `dev-dsv41` (last pushed 2026-09-11) for B300. B300 1017 cells (TP4/EP4; DSpark block 5 low-latency; `--max-running-requests 256` high-throughput) are `verified: false`. v0.5.23 enables decoder SWA bounded replay by default only for supported configurations (CUDA; no prefill/attention CP or DCP; prefill CUDA graph disabled or breakable; under DP attention only attention TP 1 with `--moe-a2a-backend` none or megamoe), so confirm the startup log line `DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder SWA bounded replay resolved to …`; it is not numerically identical to full prefill, and `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` retains full prefill when output-token logprobs must match it. It resolves `flashmla` rather than `flashmla_mega` for aggregated attention-TP layouts, and renders chat through `deepseek-recipe`. The NVIDIA NVFP4 export needs #47935, merged to main 2026-11-04 but not in v0.5.23; its config (quant_method fp8, MIXED_PRECISION, moe_quant_algo NVFP4) loads routed experts through `HybridFp8NvFp4Config`/`ModelOptFp4Config` at `297e54f`, so the generic ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE and routing-scale fixes (#45289, #45386, #44901, #44904) reach its MoE path (source inference).

insights.mechanism: Compressed-cache precision: the vLLM recipe's --kv-cache-dtype fp8 does not store the publisher-trained FP4 compressed KV; compare fp8 with nvfp4_ds_mla on FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 (DEP8) for long-context retrieval quality, KV capacity and decode latency; reject on quality loss.

insights.mechanism: Engram placement is the dominant capacity decision: ~183 GiB FP8 tables (~189 GiB with scales) per engine instance. In vLLM v0.32.0/v0.33.0 EngramConfig.cpu_offload defaults to true and an absent --engram-config becomes EngramConfig(), so every vLLM topology offloads to pinned host memory unless cpu_offload:false is set. Four independent TP2 replicas pin ~730-755 GiB and two TP4 replicas ~366-378 GiB of host memory; TP4 with cpu_offload:false keeps ~47.2 GiB of Engram per rank in HBM instead. DEP8 (DP 8 on one node) resolves dp_shared_memory on and shares one host copy through /dev/shm, which the pod must size at >= ~189 GiB; embedding_across_dp is a separate sharding setting. Measure host RAM, /dev/shm, startup time and lookup latency per layout.

insights.mechanism: Indexer logits buffer = max-num-batched-tokens x max-model-len x 2 bytes (16 GiB per rank at 8192 x 1M); cap max-model-len to the application budget and record the freed KV capacity.
